method_choice: Both methods suit this nonpolar, near-ideal pair at 1.1 atm (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 2 and 6): the flowsheet in Peng-Robinson (B2's method, its k_ij fitted to ThermoML data), the column in NRTL (the ChemSep set, tier databank) with an ideal-gas vapour. The choice is deliberate, to have two methods whose enthalpies differ at the same T and P (Peng-Robinson's departure enthalpies against NRTL's liquid heat capacities and ideal gas), so that the boundary is tested.

boundary.finds: T (and the vapour fraction) by a P-H flash in the receiving method
boundary.why_lower_bound: 278.68 K, where benzene's liquid heat-capacity record starts in CHEPTA (Thol et al. 2012 through CoolProp, its triple point): below it CHEPTA's NRTL liquid enthalpy refuses (OUT_OF_RANGE)

title: Benzene + toluene: the G1 column with half of its bottoms recycled to the feed through a mixer in the flowsheet's method
purpose: The boundary in a recycle (proposal 0015, Part I, section 3: "an adiabatic boundary in both directions and in a recycle"). Half of the bottoms crosses back into the flowsheet's method, is mixed adiabatically with the fresh feed there and crosses into the column again. At the converged recycle no energy is created or lost around the loop: the fresh feed's enthalpy flow plus the reboiler duty minus the condenser duty equals the distillate's and the bottoms product's enthalpy flows.

specs.note: the bottoms product (after the recycle split); the column's own bottoms flow is twice this

behaviour: the recycle converges (fixture boundary.recycle); the column's bottoms flow is the product's divided by 1 - 0.5
energy.imbalance_W is zero to the tolerances: the loop crosses the boundary twice per pass and loses or creates nothing
the result reports the temperature change of each crossing

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

boundary.why: the P-H flash is solved to 1e-10 K; the balance closes to the column's own tolerance

recycle.mixer: adiabatic, in the flowsheet's method, at the column's pressure
